title: Comparative analysis of metabolism in parasitic worms
protocol: Run Pathway Tools pipeline for each species using Biocyc database.
Analyze biosynthesis pathways for vitamins and amino acids.
Compare identified biosynthetic capabilities to identify auxotrophies.
Remove KEGG pathways not relevant to helminths.
Include only KEGG pathways with at least one reference pathway for a nematode or platyhelminth species.
Exclude pathways such as ‘Carbon fixation in photosynthetic organisms’ even if some enzymes are found in helminths.
Manually exclude pathways deemed irrelevant, like caffeine metabolism for most helminths studied.
Define coverage as the fraction of all reference pathway ECs annotated in a given species.
Calculate coverage for every helminth-relevant KEGG metabolic pathway.
Compare coverage separately among different groups of worms at the phylum level (platyhelminths and nematodes).
Compare coverage among subsets within platyhelminths (cestodes and trematodes).
Compare coverage among subsets within nematodes from different clades.
Define specific groups such as ‘Clade IVa-’ for comparisons.
Perform Wilcoxon tests to compare coverage between worm groups.
Correct P-values using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure for significance assignment (P<0.05).
Measure coverage diversity by calculating the coefficient of variation of pathway coverage among different worm groups.
Compare coverage diversity across all worms between different ‘superpathways’ (e.g., combining all ‘amino acid metabolism’ pathways together).
Perform Wilcoxon tests over the distribution of coefficient of variation for these comparisons.
Generate a phylogenetic tree using Ward-linkage based on the Jaccard similarity index for species clustering based on presence/absence of modules.
Generate a phylogenetic tree using Ward-linkage based on the Jaccard similarity index for species clustering based on lenient presence/absence of modules.
Species clustering based on presence/absence of ECs is performed using Ward-linkage based on the Jaccard similarity index.
Generate a phylogenetic tree to identify potential peculiarities in metabolic potential evolution among closely related species.
